drafts.email_text:
Clarification on Claims for My Child Born Last Year

Hello,

I am a working mother, and my child was born last year. I'm trying to understand what I can claim on my taxes related to my child. Could you please provide some guidance on the benefits or deductions available for new parents like me? Thank you.
drafts.judge_reason: All factual statements about relief amounts, eligibility conditions, caps, and the Parenthood Tax Rebate are directly supported by the cited SOPs.
drafts.text:
Qualifying Child Relief is $4,000 per qualifying child, and Child Relief (Disability) is $7,500 per qualifying child. To claim Qualifying Child Relief, your child must be unmarried, and must be your own child, a step-child, or legally adopted. The child must have been below 16 years old, or 16 or above and studying full-time at a university, college or other educational institution at any time during the year. The child must also not have had annual income of more than $8,000. Parents may share the relief for the same child in a proportion they agree between themselves.

For a qualifying Singaporean child born or adopted on or after 1 January 2024, Working Mother's Child Relief is a fixed amount: $8,000 for the first child, $10,000 for the second, and $12,000 for the third and each subsequent child.

You may claim Working Mother's Child Relief even if you or your husband or ex-husband has already claimed Qualifying Child Relief or Child Relief (Disability) on the same child. Qualifying Child Relief is allowed first, and Working Mother's Child Relief is limited to the remaining balance, with a combined cap of $50,000 per child.

The Parenthood Tax Rebate is a one-off rebate for tax residents, of $5,000 for the first child, $10,000 for the second, and $20,000 for the third and fourth child. Any unutilised amount is carried forward to offset your income tax in later years until it is fully used, and it may also be transferred to your spouse.

Timeframe for Objecting to a Tax Bill

I recently received a tax bill that I believe is incorrect. Could you please let me know how long I have to file an objection to it? Thank you for your assistance.
drafts.judge_reason: All factual statements (30‑day amendment window, payment due within 1 month despite objection, 30‑day refund of credit balances) are directly supported by the SOP text.
drafts.text:
If you need to make a change after receiving your tax bill, you may file an amendment using the 'Amend Tax Bill' digital service at myTax Portal within 30 days from the date on your Notice of Assessment. IRAS will review the amendment and inform you of the outcome.

Please note that filing an objection does not defer payment. Tax is due within 1 month of the date of your Notice of Assessment, and a late payment penalty applies to tax outstanding after that date even while an objection is being reviewed. If your assessment is revised, any credit balance is refunded within 30 days from the date of the amended tax bill.

drafts.label: tax_reliefs
drafts.email_text:
Enquiry on Claiming Dependants for Tax Relief

Good day,

I am writing to ask about claiming dependants for tax relief. I currently support both of my parents and my grandmother. Could you please explain how many dependants I am allowed to include when filing my taxes? Thank you for your assistance.
drafts.judge_reason: All factual statements in the draft are directly supported by SOP‑REL‑002.
drafts.text:
To claim Parent Relief, you must have supported a dependant who was 55 years of age or above, who did not have annual income of more than $8,000 in 2025, and who was living with you in the same household in Singapore. If your dependant did not live with you, the relief applies only if they stayed in Singapore for at least 8 months in the year. Qualifying dependants include parents, grandparents, parents-in-law and grandparents-in-law, as well as step-parents and adoptive parents.

You may claim the relief for up to 2 dependants. If more than one person supports the same dependant and each meets the qualifying conditions, the relief may be shared between you.

Parent Relief is $9,000 per dependant if you stay with your dependant, and $5,500 if you do not. Parent Relief (Disability) is $14,000 per dependant if you stay with your dependant, and $10,000 if you do not.

drafts.email_text:
Claiming for Child and Elderly Parent in the Same Year

Hi, I'm reaching out to understand if I can claim tax relief for both my young child and my elderly mother in the same tax year. They both rely on my support, but I am unsure about how the process works or if there are any restrictions I should be aware of. Could you please guide me on how to proceed with this? Thank you for your assistance.
drafts.judge_reason: The draft’s statement that “you may claim tax relief for both your child and your parent in the same tax year” is not directly supported by any SOP text.
drafts.text:
You may claim tax relief for both your child and your parent in the same tax year, provided you satisfy the qualifying conditions for each relief.

To claim Qualifying Child Relief for Year of Assessment 2026, all the conditions must have been met in 2025. Your child must be unmarried, and must be your own child, a step-child, or legally adopted. The child must have been below 16 years old, or 16 or above and studying full-time at a university, college or other educational institution at any time during the year. The child must also not have had annual income of more than $8,000.

Qualifying Child Relief is $4,000 per qualifying child, and Child Relief (Disability) is $7,500 per qualifying child. Parents may share the relief for the same child in a proportion they agree between themselves.

To claim Parent Relief you must have supported a dependant who was 55 years of age or above, who did not have annual income of more than $8,000 in 2025, and who was living with you in the same household in Singapore. If your dependant did not live with you, the relief applies only if they stayed in Singapore for at least 8 months in the year. Qualifying dependants include parents, grandparents, parents-in-law and grandparents-in-law, as well as step-parents and adoptive parents.

Parent Relief is $9,000 per dependant if you stay with your dependant, and $5,500 if you do not. Parent Relief (Disability) is $14,000 per dependant if you stay with your dependant, and $10,000 if you do not. You may claim the relief for up to 2 dependants. If more than one person supports the same dependant and each meets the qualifying conditions, the relief may be shared between you.
